## ELI5

<!--
Required, and it goes first. Two to five sentences of plain language for a
reader who has never opened this repository: what is wrong or missing, what
someone would notice because of it, and what "fixed" would look like from
outside. No spec numbers, no rule identifiers, no crate or verb names unless
you say in the same breath what they are. If a term below is jargon, this is
where it gets defined in ordinary words.

Write this last and put it first. If you cannot write it without the jargon,
that is usually a sign the issue itself is not yet understood.
-->

<!--
Below the ELI5, write for a reader who does know the repository. Open with one
or two sentences saying what this is and where it came from, with the link or
quotation the claim rests on. Then the sections.
-->

## What happens today

The state of the tree, measured rather than recalled: the code path, the test

case for and the case against.
-->

## Done when

Bars a verifier can check clause by clause, without you present. Each one is a

-->
